Apple Just Raised Prices Across Its Entire Lineup — Here's the Real Reason Why

thread // Jun 27, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Read more on Threads

Apple just raised the price of Apple TV by 54%. That's the biggest percentage jump of anything they sell.

On June 25, Apple raised prices on 14 products at once: every Mac, every iPad, Apple TV, both HomePods and Vision Pro. Apple actually held off for months before finally doing it.

The full list

Starting prices in the U.S., before and after, biggest jump first:

  • Apple TV: $129 → $199 (+54%)
  • Mac mini (256GB): $599 → $799 (+33%)
  • Mac Studio (M3 Ultra): $3,999 → $5,299 (+33%)
  • HomePod mini: $99 → $129 (+30%)
  • iPad: $349 → $449 (+29%)
  • iPad Air: $599 → $749 (+25%)
  • Mac Studio (M4 Max): $1,999 → $2,499 (+25%)
  • iPad mini: $499 → $599 (+20%)
  • iPad Pro: $999 → $1,199 (+20%)
  • MacBook Air: $1,099 → $1,299 (+18%)
  • MacBook Pro: $1,699 → $1,999 (+18%)
  • HomePod: $299 → $349 (+17%)
  • MacBook Neo: $599 → $699 (+17%)
  • iMac: $1,299 → $1,499 (+15%)
  • Mac mini (M4 Pro): $1,399 → $1,599 (+14%)
  • Vision Pro: $3,499 → $3,699 (+6%)

What didn't change in June: iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, Studio Display and accessories like the Apple Pencil.

Why it's happening

AI companies are buying up the memory chips (RAM and storage) that go into phones and laptops to fill their data centers. That's left less supply for regular companies like Apple, Dell and Microsoft, and memory prices shot up. Tim Cook called the demand a "100-year flood" and said the increases were unavoidable.

The products that need the most memory, like Macs and iPads, took the biggest hits. The ones that need less, like Apple Watch and AirPods, didn't move.

Update (September 2026)

It reached the iPhone. At Apple's September 9 event, the iPhone Air went up to $1,099 and the iPhone 17e to $699, $100 more each.

One correction from my original post: I listed the MacBook Air as starting at $1,000 and the MacBook Pro at $1,600. The old starting prices were $1,099 and $1,699. The percentages I posted were right.

Sources: MacRumors, 9to5Mac, CNBC, Wikipedia: iPhone Air, Wikipedia: iPhone 17e

Quick answers

Why did Apple raise prices in 2026? Because of a memory chip shortage, as AI data centers buy up the RAM and storage chips that computers and phones need.

When did Apple raise prices? On June 25, 2026, for Macs, iPads, Apple TV, HomePod and Vision Pro.

How much is the Apple TV now? $199, up from $129.

Did iPhone prices go up? Not in June. In September, Apple raised the iPhone Air to $1,099 and the iPhone 17e to $699.
